title: Booking Summer 2027 Flights to Bodrum, Dalaman, Antalya or İzmir: What Has Changed
excerpt: Checks of Ryanair’s booking site show no Bodrum or Dalaman flights on sale for summer 2027, Dalaman lost international flights in 2026 and AJet is adding German routes. A practical way to plan your 2027 resort flights.

body.text: If you usually fly to Türkiye’s Aegean or Mediterranean coast in summer, the 2027 picture looks different from recent years. Some low-cost routes have disappeared from sale, other carriers are adding flights, and Türkiye’s tourism minister has warned that fares may rise. None of this means flights will be hard to find, but it does change how to approach booking. This guide separates what is confirmed from what is only reported or forecast, and gives a simple decision framework for travellers from the UK, Ireland and Germany.
What is confirmed, reported and forecast

items: Reported, with checks: Ryanair did not include Türkiye in its summer 2027 programme. [Turizm Ekonomi](https://www.turizmekonomi.com/ryanair-drops-all-flights-to-turkiye) reported on 30 October 2026 that the airline had removed its Dublin, London Stansted and Bratislava routes to Bodrum and Dalaman. [Sözcü](https://www.sozcu.com.tr/avrupa-nin-en-buyuk-havayolu-sirketi-turkiye-yi-listesine-almadi-p374367) checked Ryanair’s booking site and found no Bodrum or Dalaman flights on sale for summer 2027, while noting that the airline had not issued a statement and that it was unclear whether the decision is final.

Announced by the airline: according to [Hürriyet Daily News](https://www.hurriyetdailynews.com/amp/ajet-to-launch-direct-flights-to-five-german-cities-next-summer-228411), AJet will fly from Dalaman to Düsseldorf, Frankfurt, Stuttgart, Hannover and Munich from April 2027, and from Bodrum to Düsseldorf, Frankfurt and Stuttgart from July 2027, each twice weekly.

Official data: State Airports Authority figures reported by [Turizm Ekonomi](https://www.turizmekonomi.com/antalya-mugla-and-izmir-lose-7500-international-flights-in-9-months) show international flights in January–September 2026 down about 13% at Dalaman, 7% at Antalya and 4% at İzmir compared with 2025, with Milas-Bodrum broadly stable. These are flight counts, not passenger numbers.

Forecast: at WTM London, Culture and Tourism Minister Mehmet Nuri Ersoy said higher fuel costs could add around $100 on average to tickets on flights of three hours or more in 2027 and that bookings may shift towards the last minute, as [reported by Turizm Ekonomi](https://www.turizmekonomi.com/mehmet-nuri-ersoy-flags-two-key-tourism-challenges-for-2027). This is a forecast, not an announced fare rise.

body.text: Demand itself has not collapsed. The [State Airports Authority (DHMİ)](https://dhmi.gov.tr/Sayfalar/Haber/havayolunda-9-ayda-1931-milyon-yolcu.aspx) reports that Antalya handled about 30.1 million passengers in January–September 2026, İzmir about 10.3 million, Dalaman about 4.6 million and Milas-Bodrum about 3.9 million. The change is in who flies where, and how much choice you have on a given route.
Step 1: Decide how flexible your airport is

The four resort airports serve different stretches of coast. Dalaman is the gateway to Fethiye, Göcek and Dalyan; Milas-Bodrum serves the Bodrum peninsula; Antalya serves Antalya, Belek, Side, Kemer and Alanya; İzmir serves Çeşme, Kuşadası and Ephesus. If you have not chosen your coast yet, our [Turkish Riviera guide](/blog/turkish-riviera-antalya-bodrum-fethiye-guide) compares them. If your hotel is fixed, compare the transfer time from a second airport before booking a cheaper flight there; a long transfer can cancel the saving.
Step 2: Compare direct and one-stop options

When a direct low-cost route disappears, the realistic alternatives are usually another carrier’s direct flight from a different home airport, a package holiday with charter seats, or a connection through Istanbul. A connection adds time, so check the total journey including the layover rather than the flight time alone, and book both legs on a single booking where possible: if the first flight is delayed, the airline is then generally responsible for rebooking you, which is not the case with separately bought tickets.
Step 3: Choose your booking timing deliberately

There is no reliable rule that booking late or early is cheaper in 2027. The minister’s comments suggest more last-minute selling, while lower capacity on some routes means popular dates can sell out early. A practical approach is to fix the parts that are scarce (school-holiday dates, a specific direct route, a particular resort) early, and keep flexibility on the parts that are not. Choosing fares that allow changes reduces the cost of being wrong.

items: Confirm that the route is actually on sale for your dates on the airline’s own site, not only listed as a route on a map.
Check the operating days: many new seasonal routes, such as AJet’s Germany services, run only twice a week.
Compare at least one alternative airport and one Istanbul connection.
Check the baggage allowance; sports equipment rules matter for golf trips, as our [Belek golf trip guide](/blog/belek-antalya-golf-trip-season-planning) explains.
Look at the season dates: some routes start in April, others not until July.
Keep a note of the booking reference and the airline’s contact route in case the schedule changes again before summer.

body.text: For the timing of the trip itself rather than the flight, our [month-by-month guide](/blog/best-time-to-visit-turkiye-month-by-month) covers weather and crowds. The flight landscape may move again before summer 2027, so treat this as a snapshot as of 9 November 2026 and re-check before you book.

seo.intent: Plan and book 2027 summer flights to Türkiye's resort airports after route changes, including Ryanair's absence and new AJet routes.
seo.uniqueValue: Separates confirmed, reported and forecast changes for 2027 resort flights and turns them into a three-step airport, routing and timing framework with a pre-payment checklist; no fare predictions presented as fact.

quality.reviewNotes: Prepared 2026-11-09. Ryanair exit presented as reported (Turizm Ekonomi, Sözcü booking-site check), no Ryanair statement exists; disputed 40/week vs 480/year figures deliberately omitted. Turizm Ekonomi headline 7,500 figure not quoted; per-airport percentages from its body (DHMİ data). DHMİ passenger totals from DHMİ page. Minister's $100 presented as forecast. Travel booking logistics only; no financial advice. Independent review recorded in the daily ledger.
